summary.en: Militant attacks continue in Jammu and Kashmir, with a recent gunbattle in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa killing 10 policemen and 18 militants, and a terror attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam injuring three jawans, one critically. Two SPOs have gone missing in Kishtwar, prompting a massive search operation, while security forces in Manipur arrested five suspected cadres of KYKL, PREPAK and PLA. Heightened security measures include NIA teams collecting samples at the Kulgam site and increased drone deployment. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantangrep fortsetter i Jammu og Kashmir, med en nylig skuddkrig i Pakistans Khyber Pakhtunkhwa som drepte 10 politifolk og 18 militante, og et terrorangrep på CRPF-personell i Kulgam som såret tre jawaner, én kritisk. To SPO-er har forsvunnet i Kishtwar, noe som har utløst en omfattende søkeoperasjon, mens sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur arresterte fem mistenkte medlemmer av KYKL, PREPAK og PLA. Økte sikkerhetstiltak inkluderer NIA-team som samler prøver på Kulgam-stedet og økt bruk av droner. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
